description.en:
# FRT

## Overview

FRT is a web-based system for processing 3D microscopy images using machine learning and deep learning methods, developed at the Laboratory of Molecular Neurodegeneration (LMN), SPbPU.

The system exposes image-processing pipelines as an online service rather than as a local script, so that microscopy data can be uploaded, queued and processed asynchronously through a browser.

## Stack

The service is built on FastAPI with Celery for asynchronous job execution, Redis as the broker/result backend, S3 for image storage, a React frontend, and Docker for deployment. These are the only technologies the sources attach to this project; no ML framework is named for it in any source.

## Results

No quantitative results are recorded for FRT in any available source. The project's `metrics` list is therefore empty — this reflects an absence of measurements in the sources, not an absence of outcomes.

## Patents

Two patent registrations are linked to this project in the CV: one for an online service for neural-network and algorithmic deconvolution of confocal fluorescence microscopy images, and one for automatic segmentation of fluorescent microspheres in confocal microscopy images. Registration numbers and dates are absent from every source, and the scans are private, so neither is recorded as canonical evidence here.

## Links

- Source code: https://github.com/IMZolin/frt-web

description.en:
# NeuroRAG

## Overview

NeuroRAG is a research project on multi-agent retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for question answering in neurobiology and medicine, developed at the Laboratory of Biomedical Imaging and Data Analysis (LABID), SPbPU.

General-purpose large language models are strong at language generation and retrieval but unreliable in specialised scientific reasoning. NeuroRAG addresses this by grounding answers in domain literature rather than in model parameters alone.

## Approach

The system retrieves over domain-specific biomedical sources — PubMed, arXiv and NCBI Gene/Protein — alongside web sources, and combines several retrieval strategies with adaptive techniques: Reciprocal Rank Fusion, LLM-based document reranking and contextual compression. Answers are produced by ensemble generation across several LLMs, followed by validation steps intended to minimise hallucinations and verify answer relevance.

## Results

Measured results are recorded as `metrics` in `project.yml` and described in full in the `neurorag` publication record. In summary: on nine MMLU biomedical subsets the system ranked first or tied for first in six categories, with peak accuracies of 99.0% (Medical Genetics, tied with GPT-4.1), 94.1% (High School Chemistry) and 92.8% (Clinical Knowledge), exceeding BioMistral by 20–41 percentage points on every subset. On the open-ended PubMedQA benchmark (n=50) it more than doubled the BERTScore of a FlashRAG Naive RAG baseline (0.425 versus 0.206). In a structured blind evaluation, 13 domain specialists selected NeuroRAG as the best response 103 times out of 160 evaluated responses — 72.5% of decisive preferences, after excluding nine ties and nine "all inadequate" verdicts.

On the curated PubMed Summary QA free-text benchmark NeuroRAG reached a cosine similarity of 0.759 — statistically tied with Mistral Large and Llama 3.3 70B, and behind GPT-4o at 0.795.

## Status

The work is described in a manuscript that is currently under review; see the `neurorag` publication record for its authors, venue and status.

## Links

- Source code: https://github.com/Biomed-imaging-lab/NeuroRAG
- Web service: https://neurorag.vladimirskvortsov.com

# NeuroRAG

## Обзор

NeuroRAG — исследовательский проект по мультиагентной генерации с извлечением (RAG) для ответов на вопросы по нейробиологии и медицине, разработанный в Лаборатории анализа биомедицинских изображений и данных (ЛАБИД), СПбПУ.

В русскоязычных источниках проект описан как «ИИ-ассистент для нейробиологов» на основе мультиагентной архитектуры LLM и RAG с доступом к PubMed, NCBI и arXiv.

## Подход

Система выполняет поиск по предметным биомедицинским источникам — PubMed, arXiv и NCBI Gene/Protein — а также по веб-источникам, объединяя несколько стратегий извлечения с адаптивными методами: Reciprocal Rank Fusion, переранжирование документов с помощью LLM и контекстное сжатие. Ответ формируется ансамблем из нескольких LLM с последующими шагами валидации, снижающими число галлюцинаций и проверяющими релевантность ответа.

## Результаты

Измеренные результаты записаны в поле `metrics` файла `project.yml`. Кратко: на девяти биомедицинских подмножествах MMLU система заняла первое или разделила первое место в шести категориях с пиковой точностью 99.0% (Medical Genetics, наравне с GPT-4.1), 94.1% (High School Chemistry) и 92.8% (Clinical Knowledge), превзойдя BioMistral на 20–41 процентного пункта на каждом подмножестве. На открытом бенчмарке PubMedQA (n=50) показатель BERTScore более чем вдвое превысил базовое решение FlashRAG Naive RAG (0.425 против 0.206). В слепой экспертной оценке 13 специалистов признали ответ NeuroRAG лучшим 103 раза из 160 оценённых ответов — 72.5% решающих предпочтений, после исключения девяти ничьих и девяти вердиктов «все ответы неадекватны».

На бенчмарке PubMed Summary QA косинусное сходство составило 0.759 — статистически наравне с Mistral Large и Llama 3.3 70B и ниже GPT-4o (0.795).

Примечание: эти результаты приведены по англоязычной рукописи (см. поле `metrics` в `project.yml` и запись публикации `neurorag`); русскоязычной версии аннотации в источниках нет.

## Статус

Работа описана в рукописи, находящейся на рецензировании; авторы, издание и статус указаны в записи публикации `neurorag`.

## Ссылки

- Веб-сервис: https://neurorag.vladimirskvortsov.com

description.en:
# TriDeFusion

## Overview

TriDeFusion is a research line on deep-learning-based restoration and denoising of 3D fluorescence microscopy images, developed across two laboratories: the Laboratory of Molecular Neurodegeneration (LMN), SPbPU (TriDeFusion v1) and the Laboratory of Biomedical Imaging and Data Analysis (LABID), SPbPU (TriDeFusion-v2).

Fluorescence microscopy images are frequently degraded by noise and distortions that complicate downstream analysis. TriDeFusion addresses this by combining classical and learned denoising techniques rather than relying on a single method.

## TriDeFusion (v1)

The first version combines Noise2Noise (N2N) with Non-Local Means (NLM) filtering for 3D image denoising. On synthetic data it achieved up to a 54% reduction in RMSE and a 20% increase in PSNR compared to an N2N-UNet baseline; on real data it reduced noise mean intensity by over 50% and noise variance by 33%. This work was presented as "TriDeFusion: Enhanced denoising algorithm for 3D fluorescence microscopy images integrating modified Noise2Noise and Non-local means" at IEEE SIBIRCON 2024 (see the `tridefusion-v1` publication).

## TriDeFusion-v2

The second version extends the approach into a hybrid spatial-frequency restoration design: a lightweight attention-based CNN family (RAUDen), Noise2Noise knowledge distillation into a smaller distilled variant (RAUDen-Lite, -40% parameters and inference time), and a locally adaptive, CUDA-accelerated wavelet-domain refinement module (8x speedup). This work is described in "TriDeFusion-v2: Distilled Hybrid Residual Attention Denoising and Wavelet Filtering", currently under review in a Q1 journal (see the `tridefusion-v2` publication).

## Code

Source code: https://github.com/Biomed-imaging-lab/TriDeFusion

title.en: NeuroRAG: A Multi-Agent Model for Neurobiological Question Answering

description.en:
# NeuroRAG: A Multi-Agent Model for Neurobiological Question Answering

## Abstract

**Objective:** Large Language Models (LLMs) perform well in general language tasks but remain prone to factual errors and weak domain-specific reasoning in neurobiology and medicine. This study aims to improve the reliability of biomedical question answering.

**Methods:** We developed NeuroRAG, a multi-agent retrieval-augmented generation framework that combines domain-specific and web-based retrieval, adaptive document filtering, multi-LLM answer generation, and post-generation validation. Its performance was evaluated on nine biomedical MMLU subsets, a free-text PubMed Summary QA dataset, PubMedQA, and a blinded expert assessment.

**Results:** NeuroRAG ranked first or tied for first on six of nine MMLU subsets and exceeded the biomedical baseline model by 20–41 percentage points across all subsets. On PubMed Summary QA, it achieved competitive semantic similarity relative to leading general-purpose LLMs and substantially outperformed the biomedical baseline. On PubMedQA, NeuroRAG more than doubled the BERTScore of a Naive RAG baseline. In the expert evaluation, 13 specialists assessed 160 responses to 12 neurobiological questions; NeuroRAG received 103 of 160 total selections and 72.5% of decisive model preferences after excluding ties and inadequate responses.

**Conclusion:** NeuroRAG demonstrates that structured multi-source retrieval, adaptive filtering, ensemble generation, and validation can improve the quality and grounding of biomedical question answering compared with standalone LLMs and simple RAG pipelines. The framework provides a reproducible tool for source-grounded scientific information support in neurobiology and biomedicine.

## Keywords

neuroscience; multi-agent generation; large language model; retrieval-augmented generation; RAG; LLM

title.en: TriDeFusion: Enhanced denoising algorithm for 3D fluorescence microscopy images integrating modified Noise2Noise and Non-local means

description.en:
## Abstract

Fluorescence microscopy is a technique for obtaining images of luminous objects of small size. It is widely used in fields ranging from materials science to neurobiology. Fluorescence microscopy has several advantages over other forms of microscopy, offering high sensitivity and specificity. However, it often results in images with noise and distortions, complicating subsequent analysis. This paper introduces the TriDeFusion algorithm for 3D image denoising, integrating Non-Local Means (NLM) and Modified Noise2Noise (N2N) techniques. Our results show that TriDeFusion significantly improves image quality, particularly in preserving details while reducing noise. In experiments with synthetic data, the combined methods outperformed individual approaches in both Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) metrics, achieving up to a 54% reduction in RMSE and a 20% increase in PSNR. For real data, our algorithm demonstrated a significant reduction of noise mean intensity by over 50% and variance by 33%, confirming its robustness and effectiveness across different noise levels and data types.

title.en: TriDeFusion-v2: Distilled Hybrid Residual Attention Denoising and Wavelet Filtering

description.en:
# TriDeFusion-v2: Distilled Hybrid Residual Attention Denoising and Wavelet Filtering

## Abstract

Fluorescence microscopy is widely used to visualize biological structures, but acquired images are often degraded by noise, low signal-to-noise ratios, and limited spatial resolution. Recent deep learning–based restoration methods can achieve high reconstruction quality, but large convolutional and transformer-based architectures may impose substantial computational costs and limit their deployment on resource-constrained systems. In this work, we present TriDeFusion-v2 (TDF2), a hybrid spatial–frequency restoration framework that combines a lightweight attention-based CNN, Noise2Noise knowledge distillation, and locally adaptive wavelet-domain refinement. The proposed design separates learned spatial reconstruction from coefficient-level frequency refinement, enabling local suppression of residual high-frequency noise while preserving fine biological structures. Extensive experiments on synthetic tubular and calcium-imaging data, as well as real fluorescence microscopy acquisitions, demonstrate that TDF2 achieves competitive or superior restoration quality relative to established and recent baselines while substantially reducing model complexity and inference time. Real-data experiments further demonstrate improvements in background suppression, signal-to-noise characteristics, and structural sharpness in the absence of clean Ground Truth (GT) images. These results indicate that TDF2 provides a favorable quality–efficiency trade-off for large-scale fluorescence microscopy processing and resource-constrained biomedical imaging pipelines. Our code is available at https://github.com/Biomed-imaging-lab/TriDeFusion

## Keywords

Denoising, microscopy, neuroimaging, neural network, optimization, self-supervised learning, transformers, wavelet.
